user.title: Set Up Auto Arm
user.description: Quick setup follows the [recommended recipe]({recipe_url}) and only asks for the alarm panel and the entities it uses, with sensible defaults for everything else. Advanced setup shows the full set of options up front.

quick_setup.title: Set Up Auto Arm
quick_setup.description: Follows the [recommended recipe]({recipe_url}), with a bedtime sensor, a calendar for vacations, and arming away when everyone is out. Only the alarm panel is required, the rest can be added later.

data.time_of_day_armed_night: Bedtime - Times of the Day Sensor
data.person_entities: Presence - People for Occupancy Based Arming

data_description.alarm_panel: No alarm panel yet? [Create a virtual one]({alarm_panel_help_url}), or in Home Assistant go to Settings → Devices & Services → Helpers → **+ Create Helper** → Template → **Alarm control panel**. Give it a name and submit; every other field is optional.
data_description.calendar_entities: Calendars are needed to drive the Armed Vacation state, or if presence is unavailable or unreliable for working out occupancy. Calendars can also set any armed state, so can override other diurnal, bedtime or occupancy controls. No calendar yet? [Create a local calendar]({calendar_help_url}), or go to Settings → Devices & Services → **+ Add Integration** → **Local calendar**. Give it a name and leave 'Create empty calendar' selected.
data_description.time_of_day_armed_night: A Times of the Day sensor that's on for bedtime every day. The alarm is held at Armed Night while it's on. No bedtime sensor yet? [Create one]({bedtime_help_url}), or go to Settings → Devices & Services → Helpers → **+ Create Helper** → **Time of the Day**. Give it a name and set an After/Before time for your usual bedtime window.
data_description.person_entities: Whether or not all of these people are home drives the Armed Away, Armed Home and Disarmed states. Somebody missing? [Add a new person]({person_help_url}), or go to Settings → People → **+ Add Person**. Give them a name; linking a user account is optional.

data.calendar_occupancy_override_states: Calendar based alarm states presence can override
data.calendar_occupancy_ends_away: Coming home ends Away and Vacation events on their last day

data_description.occupied_trigger: Re-evaluate the alarm state when a person arrives home
data_description.unoccupied_trigger: Re-evaluate the alarm state when a person leaves home
data_description.calendar_occupancy_override_states: When a calendar event sets one of these states, occupancy changes (arrivals and departures) can still update the alarm state. For example, if the calendar says Disarmed but everyone leaves, it will switch to Armed Away.
data_description.calendar_occupancy_ends_away: When someone comes home on the day an Armed Away or Armed Vacation calendar event is due to end, the event ends then rather than at its end time, and the alarm goes to the state set for when a calendar event ends. Applies to one-off events as well as recurring ones.

sun_options.name: Diurnal - Sun
sun_options.description: Morning and evening are based on sunrise and sunset times with the extra earliest/latest bounds set below. The triggers re-evaluate the alarm state at morning and evening, and are ignored during bedtime. Auto switches a trigger off on any day with a Disarmed, Armed Home or Armed Night calendar event. The earliest and latest times are most useful when no Times of the Day sensor or calendar is used for bedtime.

data.occupancy_default_day: Occupied state between morning and evening
data.occupancy_default_after_bedtime: Occupied state between bedtime and morning
data.occupancy_default_night: Occupied state between evening and bedtime

data_description.occupancy_default_after_bedtime: For when bedtime ends before morning. It has no use without a bedtime sensor.
data_description.occupancy_default_night: Set this to Armed Home as a pre-bedtime default if a Times of the Day sensor or calendar sets Armed Night for bedtime, as in the [recommended recipe]({recipe_url}). If nothing sets Armed Night for bedtime that day, neither a bedtime sensor nor a calendar event, it's Armed Night from evening.
data_description.sunrise_trigger: Re-evaluate the alarm state at morning
data_description.sunrise_earliest: Morning is no earlier than this time, however early the sun rises
data_description.sunrise_latest: Morning is no later than this time, however late the sun rises
data_description.sunset_trigger: Re-evaluate the alarm state at evening
data_description.sunset_earliest: Evening is no earlier than this time, however early the sun sets
data_description.sunset_latest: Evening is no later than this time, however late the sun sets

button_options.name: Buttons
button_options.description: Physical buttons to set an alarm state, or to reset it to whatever Auto Arm works out. Button entities and binary sensors both work. Each can have a delay before it acts, such as time to get out of the door after arming away.

data_description.sentence_arm: English sentences for Home Assistant's built-in Assist agent, such as 'arm the alarm', 'arm the alarm in night mode' and 'why is the alarm armed'.
data_description.sentence_disarm: Adds 'disarm the alarm'. Warning: no code is asked for, so anyone who can talk to Assist, on a voice satellite or in the chat, can disarm the alarm.

data_description.notify_enabled: Enable notifications for alarm state changes
data_description.notify_action: Home Assistant action (service) to use to notify
data_description.notify_targets: List of addresses or notify entities to notify, can be left blank for Supernotify
data_description.notify_data: Extra data passed to the notification action, such as actions or a channel for a mobile app notification. Anything set here is overridden by a matching key in a YAML notify profile.

time_of_day_options.name: Advanced - Times of the Day Sensor
time_of_day_options.description: Times of the Day sensors for the other alarm states, each setting its state while it's on, in the same way as the bedtime sensor. When a sensor turns off, the calendar event end settings under Advanced apply.

data.use_alarm_service: Change state using the alarm panel's actions
data.calendar_armed_end_mode: When a calendar arming override ends
data.calendar_disarmed_end_mode: When a calendar disarming override ends

data_description.use_alarm_service: Call the alarm_control_panel arm and disarm actions instead of setting the state directly. Needed for panels such as Alarmo that do their own processing, like arming child areas. If the panel requires a code, set it below.
data_description.panel_code: Code for Auto Arm to give the alarm panel's actions when arming or disarming, if the panel needs one. It is stored encrypted and never shown again. Leave blank to keep the code already stored.
data_description.calendar_armed_end_mode: Auto goes by occupancy and sun, or by occupancy alone on days the sunrise and sunset triggers are off. By occupancy and sun works the state out from who's home and whether it's day or night. By occupancy disarms, or arms away if everyone is out.
data_description.calendar_disarmed_end_mode: Auto goes by occupancy and sun, or by occupancy alone on days the sunrise and sunset triggers are off. By occupancy and sun works the state out from who's home and whether it's day or night. By occupancy arms home, or away if everyone is out.

yaml_core_config_deprecated.title: YAML core configuration is deprecated
yaml_core_config_deprecated.description: Core AutoArm settings (alarm_panel, occupancy, calendars) have been migrated to the UI config entry. Remove these from your YAML configuration and use the UI to manage them. Advanced settings (transitions, buttons, notify, diurnal, rate_limit) can remain in YAML.

panel_code_required.title: Alarm panel needs a code
panel_code_required.description: The alarm panel {panel} asks for a code, and Auto Arm has none to give it, so arming or disarming may fail. Set **Alarm panel code** in the Advanced section of the Auto Arm options, or a default code in the alarm panel entity's own settings, or switch off the code requirement in the panel's integration.
